title: Reject a bad username with an unchecked exception that names the user

blocks.text: The page's first custom exception is an unchecked `InvalidUserException` that carries the id of the user whose data was wrong. Write it, and use it.

items: Complete `InvalidUserException` (it extends `RuntimeException`): the constructor `InvalidUserException(String message, String userId)` and the getter `getUserId()`. The id is a `final` field.

Write `UserValidator.validateUsername(String userId, String username)`. It returns normally for a usable username and otherwise throws `InvalidUserException` with the message `Username cannot be null or empty` and the given `userId`.

rows: throws `InvalidUserException`, message `Username cannot be null or empty`, `getUserId()` is `"u7"`

blocks.text: A handler may read the message through `getMessage()` or print the exception, so decide where the message has to live. Think about every way a username can be unusable, not only `""`.

cases.says: An empty username is rejected with an InvalidUserException that carries the user id, and a valid one passes.
The message is passed to the superclass, so getMessage() and toString() both show it.
A username of only whitespace is as empty as "".
A null username gets the same InvalidUserException, not a NullPointerException.

concepts: A custom exception extends Exception to be checked or RuntimeException to be unchecked.
The message and the cause go to the superclass constructor, not into fields of your own.
